title: Splice runtime todo & quick notes
content:
Morning drop-in notes (grabbed coffee, forgot to change terminal tab). Quick brain dump so I don't lose the micro-ideas.

Today goals (top 3):
- Stabilize the p99 regression on short seqs (investigate recent change to the KV eviction window).
- Get a reliable local repro for the tiny-batch spike (need consistent input generator + seed).
- Sketch a tiny patch for prefetch threshold to try on canary.

Observations / current hypotheses:
- P99 spikes seem correlated with sequences < 64 tokens + cold kv cache. Hypothesis: eviction threshold too aggressive causes extra recompute for many small requests.
- CPU-side scheduling jitter when batching mixes long/short sequences; suspect the scheduler weights by input length incorrectly after the batching refactor.
- One-off tail spikes appear ~11:32 UTC yesterday, coincides with autoscaler churn on node pool A. Possibly interaction: node removal -> rebalancing -> transient KV misses.

Quick repro plan (local):
1) script: scripts/repro/generate-shortseq-load --seed 31415 --qps 200 --duration 120 --model tnt-7b
2) start runtime locally with env: RUNTIME_DEBUG_KV=1 RUNTIME_PREFETCH=0.3 RUNTIME_BATCHER_DEBUG=1
3) attach perf: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60; sudo perf report (focus on syscalls and futex wake)
4) capture traces: curl -X POST localhost:8080/trace/start && run load && curl -X POST localhost:8080/trace/stop > /tmp/trace.json

Commands I will run (copy-paste friendly):
- ./scripts/start-local-runtime --config=local-debug.yaml 
- ./scripts/repro/generate-shortseq-load --seed 31415 --qps 200 --duration 120 --model tnt-7b 
- sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 120; sudo perf report --stdio > /tmp/perf-report.txt

Quick notes on KV cache eviction idea:
- Current: eviction window = 30s, max-entries-per-shard = 1024 (static)
- Try: dynamic window = min(30s, 2 * average-req-latency) and adaptive entries-per-shard based on active prefixes.
- Risk: over-allocating entries will increase memory and maybe more memcpy on GPU handoff. Start conservative: entries +10% on canary.

Canary experiment plan (small):
- Canary group: dedicated pool of 2 rtx6000 nodes, route 1% of traffic for 3h.
- Change: eviction_window -> dynamic (patch branch: runtime/evict-dynamic-1023).
- Metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, mem usage, evictions/sec.
- Rollback: automatic if p99 > baseline + 15% for 10m.

Open questions / things to ask team:
- @Ishaan: do we have fine-grained autoscaler logs for node pool A around 11:30 UTC? Need exact event ids.
- @Diego: any reason we still have static entries-per-shard? I remember there was a perf concern with resizing maps.
- Is there a cheap way to shadow the prefetch heuristic without changing production state (i.e., simulate prefetch decisions in tracing)?

Small triage notes (tickets):
- RUNTIME-4521: p99 spike after batching refactor — assigned to me.
- RUNTIME-4678: nvlink timeout on dedicated nodes — low freq, escalate if reproduces.
- RUNTIME-4720: odd mem growth during long-lived chat sessions — add slab histograms.

Things to try today (todo list):
- [ ] get local repro working end-to-end (generate load + perf + trace).
- [ ] prototype dynamic eviction patch + unit tests.
- [ ] run small canary in staging (1% traffic) if local repro shows improvement.
- [ ] add histogram logging for KV entry lifetime (count by bucket).
- [ ] follow up with infra about autoscaler events (Ishaan).
- [ ] doc short writeup for SRE handoff if we roll canary.

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Keep the test seed stable across runs.
- When collecting perf, set CPU affinity to reduce noise. Use taskset -c 4-11 for runtime process.
- If repro fails, reduce concurrency to 100 qps and rerun.

Tiny idea to explore (low effort):
- Add probabilistic retention: keep frequently-seen prefixes with 95% chance, others aged faster. Could be a middle-ground between static and full LRU.
- Benefit: less rewarm for heavy hitters. Cost: more bookkeeping on hot paths.

Meeting notes to paste into the triage thread later:
- "Working on p99 regression: suspected KV eviction + mixed-length batch scheduling. Local repro in progress; will canary dynamic eviction with tight rollback rules. Pinged infra for autoscaler events. Will post perf traces by EOD."

End-of-day acceptance criteria:
- reproducible load (perf + trace) captured OR follow-up documented + owner assigned.
